namedVariations.name: Corki front-to-back · KT Rolster
namedVariations.note: Same start and follow-up: Nautilus and Wukong start the fight, Olaf dives behind them, and Orianna and Corki follow up from range. Three frontliners (Olaf, Wukong, Nautilus) make it read front-to-back rather than pick: Corki deals sustained damage from behind instead of catches between fights. Lost to BNK FearX at the Demacia Cup (26.18). One game, so it is documented as a variation.

namedVariations.name: Ezreal front-to-back · Cloud9
namedVariations.note: Alistar starts the fight, Renekton and Naafiri dive behind him, and Orianna and Ezreal follow up from range. Like KT Rolster's draft it reads front-to-back rather than pick, with Ezreal poking from behind; Naafiri is a second diver instead of a catch jungler, and the comp check flags little tank damage. Lost to FURIA at the Worlds Play-In (26.20). One game, so it is documented as a variation.

namedVariations.name: Jarvan IV start · FURIA
namedVariations.note: The same coordinated dive: Jarvan IV starts the fight, as in BNK FearX's filed game, Ambessa and Ahri go in with him and Kalista and Renata follow. Tradeoffs: Jarvan IV is the only frontliner, short range and weak waveclear. Lost to Cloud9 at the Worlds Play-In (26.20). One game, so it is documented as a variation.

namedVariations.name: Wukong start · HANJIN BRION
namedVariations.note: The same coordinated dive: Wukong starts the fight, as in Cloud9's filed game, Olaf and Locke go in with him and Kalista and Renata follow. Olaf and Wukong are the frontline, like Renekton and Skarner in the main comp; Locke's damage replaces Akali's. Tradeoffs: short range and weak waveclear. Beat Team WE at the Demacia Cup (26.18). One game, so it is documented as a variation.

namedVariations.name: Peel + poke · BNK FearX
namedVariations.note: Still plays around Yunara, with stronger disengage and layered damage: Poppy and Lulu peel, Cassiopeia zones the front of the fight and Jayce adds poke. One frontliner (Poppy) and no on-demand engage, so the team waits for the enemy to come in. BNK picked Cassiopeia first, then Yunara and Lulu.

namedVariations.name: Ryze variation · BNK FearX
namedVariations.note: BNK's Yunara + Lulu draft in the Demacia final, where Team WE banned Cassiopeia. Lee Sin and Ryze trade the frontline and peel for mobility and side-lane pressure: no frontliner and no on-demand engage. BNK took Lee Sin, Yunara and Lulu in the first rotation.

namedVariations.name: Galio engage · Karmine Corp
namedVariations.note: Adds the proactive engage the BNK drafts lack: Galio starts fights and is the frontline, Qiyana catches and Ryze pressures a side lane. Drafted the other way round: Karmine Corp picked second and took Lulu and Yunara with its last two picks.

namedVariations.name: Galio + Wukong engage · LYON
namedVariations.note: Keeps Yunara's protection and adds the engage and frontline the core lacks: Galio and Wukong both start fights and stand in front, and Galio peels beside Lulu. Syndra adds catch and burst from behind. LYON picked first and took Wukong first, then Galio, Syndra, Yunara and Lulu. One game, so it is documented as a variation, not an archetype of its own.

namedVariations.name: Galio engage · Team WE
namedVariations.note: Same Lucian + Milio bot lane and the same short fights before items, but Galio is both the engage and the protection: he starts fights, is the only frontliner and peels with Milio, where the main comp has a stable top lane and Vi's point-click pick. Qiyana and Ahri find the catches. Tradeoffs: no lane that holds on its own, little tank damage, short range, and it falls off late. One game, so it is documented as a variation, not a comp of its own.

namedVariations.name: Diana + Yunara · Movistar KOI
namedVariations.note: Same Gnar top and Vi jungle and the same short fights around the jungle, but Diana gives the comp a second fight start beside Vi: two melee divers who go in together, where the main comp relies on Vi alone. Diana's magic damage also mixes the damage profile (about 58% physical, against 78% for the main comp). Yunara + Lulu replace Lucian + Milio, so the bot lane leans later and only Lulu peels. Tradeoffs: short range, Gnar the only frontliner, and a weaker early game than the main comp. Movistar KOI took Vi, Yunara and Lulu in the first rotation, then Gnar and Diana. One game, so it is documented as a variation, not a comp of its own.

namedVariations.name: Ornn + Jarvan IV engage · Shopify Rebellion
namedVariations.note: Same Yunara + Lulu bot lane, but Ornn and Jarvan IV start fights in front of it instead of K'Sante and Anivia holding space, which covers the main comp's missing on-demand engage. Locke trades Anivia's zone control for close-range damage and costs waveclear. FlyQuest's Ornn, Nocturne and Syndra lineup plays the same way: Ornn starts, Syndra and Yunara deal damage from behind.

namedVariations.name: Jax + Aphelios · LGD Gaming
namedVariations.note: Keeps the plan: Skarner starts, Jax and Locke go in with him, Karma speeds the dive. Tradeoffs: Sivir's team-wide speed-up is gone, Jax is a side-lane diver rather than a second frontliner beside Skarner, and Aphelios needs items, so the comp gives up its early edge and leans later.

held.name: Dive + Skirmish · Akali
held.note: Anyone's Legend's Neeko-started dive and CTBC Flying Oyster's Olaf + Lee Sin skirmish dive share Olaf and Akali but start their fights differently, so their strategic identity is not established yet. Reconsider when another team plays a comparable Olaf + Akali dive.

held.name: Front-to-back + Split · Yunara
held.note: Team WE's Yorick lineup and FURIA's Olaf lineup share a Sejuani + Akali + Yunara + Lulu core, but Yorick's split pressure and Olaf's skirmishing win differently, so FURIA's game does not confirm the split comp. Reconsider when another team plays a comparable split-push lineup.

held.note: Zaahen, Sejuani and Sylas around Yunara + Lulu; kept apart from Team WE's Yorick and Akali split lineup, which it does not play like.

families.name: Yunara protection
families.note: Comps that protect Yunara with Lulu, each with its own plan: a pick comp (Pantheon and Syndra), protect and front-to-back, and protect.

archetypes.name: Protect · Yunara
archetypes.plan: Every lineup here is drafted so Yunara can carry the fights. Most keep her alive with peel and someone in front and let the enemy come in; each variation shows which of those jobs it keeps, replaces or gives up.
archetypes.coreNote: Orianna and Lulu peel and Orianna zones the front of the fight; Olaf is the only frontliner and Xin Zhao catches. No on-demand engage, so the team waits for the enemy to come in.

members.name: Protect + front-to-back · Team Vitality
members.note: K'Sante holds the front while Anivia's wall and Lulu peel, the closest variation to the core plan. Anivia is a second ranged threat: the comp check names her as the carry to keep alive, though Yunara is still the main damage. Naafiri adds a backline dive. No on-demand engage, so the team waits for the enemy to come in.

review.why: Filed with Protect + front-to-back · Yunara. The comp check reads it as front-to-back + scaling, not protect: Ornn and Jarvan IV start fights in front of Yunara instead of waiting, with less peel around her. It may be a proactive-engage way to run this plan or a separate front-to-back archetype, so it is not counted as a variation until that is decided.
